title.zh: 卷253 列傳四十 莫洛 陈福 王之鼎 李兴元 陈启泰 陈丹赤 葉映榴
title.en: Volume 253 Biographies 40: Mo Luo, Chen Fu, Wang Zhiding, Li Xingyuan, Chen Qitai, Chen Danchi, Ye Yingliu
title.raw: 卷253 列傳四十 莫洛 陈福 王之鼎 李兴元 陈启泰 陈丹赤 葉映榴

sentences.zh: =莫洛=莫洛，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲正紅旗人，世居呼納赫魯。

translations.literal: =Mo Luo= Mo Luo, of the Irgen Gioro clan, a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner, whose family had long resided at Hunakehulu.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Luo, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Red Banner whose family had long lived at Hunakehulu.

sentences.zh: 祖溫察，太祖時來歸。

translations.literal: His ancestor Wenchai submitted during the time of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Wenchai came over to the Qing side in the reign of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 莫洛初授刑部理事官，累遷工部郎中。

translations.literal: Mo Luo was first appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and was promoted in succession to director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Luo began as a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and rose through the ranks to become a director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, he was promoted to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1667 he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 七年，出為山西陝西總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he went out as governor-general of Shanxi and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Governor-General of Shanxi and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 陝西飢，平涼、臨洮、鞏昌、西安、延安、鳳翔、漢中、興安諸府州多逋賦，有司令現戶均輸，民苦之，奏請蠲免。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered famine; Pingliang, Lintao, Gongchang, Xi'an, Yan'an, Fengxiang, Hanzhong, Xing'an and other prefectures and departments had much overdue tax; there were officials who ordered present households to pay equally; the people found it bitter, and he memorialized requesting exemption.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Shaanxi, many prefectures and departments—including Pingliang, Lintao, Gongchang, Xi'an, Yan'an, Fengxiang, Hanzhong, and Xing'an—were heavily in arrears on land tax. Some local officials had ordered current households to share the burden evenly, to the people's great distress. Mo Luo memorialized for tax remission.

sentences.zh: 迭疏清釐加派、火耗諸弊。

translations.literal: He submitted memorials repeatedly to clear away the abuses of additional levies, meltage and wear surcharges, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He sent repeated memorials to root out abuses such as extra surcharges and unauthorized meltage-and-wear fees.

sentences.zh: 八年，輔政大臣鼇拜獲譴，法司以莫洛附鼇拜，請逮問，詔以能任事，貸勿治，仍留任。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the regent Oboi was punished; the judiciary took Mo Luo as having attached himself to Oboi and requested that he be arrested and questioned; the edict said that because he was capable in his duties he was pardoned and not prosecuted, and he was still retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1669, after the disgraced regent Oboi fell, the judicial authorities charged Mo Luo with having sided with him and asked that he be arrested and tried. The emperor ruled that his proven ability warranted pardon; he was not prosecuted and kept his post.

sentences.zh: 九年，計典，仍以前罪奪職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at the evaluation of officials, he was still deprived of office on the former charge.
translations.idiomatic: At the 1670 triennial review, however, he was again stripped of office on the earlier charge.

sentences.zh: 陝西民籥留，甘肅巡撫劉鬥同，提督張勇、柏永馥等疏言莫洛清正，在官有善政，乞留以慰民望。

translations.literal: The people of Shaanxi petitioned to keep him; Gansu governor Liu Dou, together with provincial military commanders Zhang Yong, Bai Yongfu and others, memorialized that Mo Luo was upright and clear, that in office he had good policies, and begged that he be retained to comfort the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shaanxi petitioned to keep him in office. Gansu Governor Liu Dou, together with Provincial Military Commander Zhang Yong, Bai Yongfu, and others, memorialized that Mo Luo was upright, had governed well, and should be retained to satisfy popular expectation.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「簡用督撫，原以綏輯地方，愛養百姓。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed, saying: "In selecting governors and governors-general, the original purpose is to pacify and put in order the regions and to cherish and nurture the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Governors and governors-general are appointed to bring order to the provinces and care for the people.

sentences.zh: 莫洛既能得民，其免處分，供職如故。

translations.literal: Since Mo Luo has been able to win the people, let him be exempted from punishment and continue in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Since Mo Luo has won the people's trust, let his punishment be waived and let him continue in office as before.

sentences.zh: 」俄擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he was promoted to minister of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was promoted to Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十三年，吳三桂等奏請撤籓，上敕廷臣議，皆主勿徙，惟莫洛與米思翰、明珠議撤。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Wu Sangui and others memorialized requesting the abolition of the feudatories; the emperor ordered the court ministers to deliberate; all advocated not moving them, only Mo Luo together with Misihan and Mingzhu advocated abolition.
translations.idiomatic: In 1674, Wu Sangui and the other feudatory princes petitioned to surrender their domains. The emperor ordered the court to debate the matter. Most ministers opposed relocation, but Mo Luo, Misihan, and Mingzhu argued for abolishing the feudatories.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，四川提督鄭蛟麟等叛應之。

translations.literal: Sangui rebelled; Sichuan provincial military commander Zheng Jiaolin and others rebelled in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui rose in rebellion, Sichuan Provincial Military Commander Zheng Jiaolin and others joined him.

sentences.zh: 二月，命莫洛經略陝西，拜武英殿大學士，仍管兵部，賜以敕印，既至，策遣諸軍徵四川。

translations.literal: In the second month, Mo Luo was ordered to serve as grand coordinator of Shaanxi, was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, still directed the Ministry of War, and was granted the imperial seal; once he arrived, he planned and dispatched the armies to campaign in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was appointed to coordinate military affairs in Shaanxi, made a Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory while retaining charge of the Ministry of War, and granted an imperial commission seal. On arrival he drew up plans and dispatched the armies against Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時蛟麟兵據廣元百丈關，莫洛遣都統馬一寶、將軍席卜臣赴漢中，副都統科爾寬赴廣元，擊賊。

translations.literal: At the time Jiaolin's troops held Baizhang Pass at Guangyuan; Mo Luo sent commandant Ma Yibao and general Xibuchen to Hanzhong, and vice commandant Ke'erkuang to Guangyuan, to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaolin's forces then held Baizhang Pass at Guangyuan. Mo Luo sent Commandant Ma Yibao and General Xibuchen to Hanzhong and Vice Commandant Ke'erkuang to Guangyuan to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 十月，蛟麟將何德成犯寧羌，為官軍所敗，還奔四川，莫洛因遣提督王輔臣駐其地。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Jiaolin's general He Decheng invaded Ningqiang, was defeated by the government troops, and fled back to Sichuan; Mo Luo thereupon sent provincial military commander Wang Fuchen to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Jiaolin's general He Decheng attacked Ningqiang, was beaten by government forces, and fled back into Sichuan. Mo Luo then sent Provincial Military Commander Wang Fuchen to hold the area.

sentences.zh: 踰月，蛟麟將彭時亨复據七盤、百丈諸關，劫略陽糧艘，截陸運棧道。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Jiaolin's general Peng Shiheng again seized Qipan, Baizhang and other passes, plundered grain boats at Lueyang, and cut the overland transport plank road.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Jiaolin's general Peng Shiheng reoccupied Qipan, Baizhang, and other passes, raided grain convoys at Lueyang, and severed the overland supply route.

sentences.zh: 廣元軍缺餉兩月矣，總兵王懷忠所部潰散，而輔臣亦陰懷異志。

translations.literal: The Guangyuan army had lacked pay for two months; regional commander Wang Huaizhong's troops had scattered in rout, and Fuchen also secretly harbored a different intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangyuan army had gone without pay for two months. Regional Commander Wang Huaizhong's troops had broken and scattered, and Fuchen was already secretly disloyal.

sentences.zh: 輔臣故與莫洛有郄，奉檄使隨徵，益怏怏，藉口戎備寡，莫洛益以騎兵二千，少之；

translations.literal: Fuchen had long had a grudge against Mo Luo; ordered by commission to follow the campaign, he grew all the more resentful; taking as his pretext that military preparations were few, Mo Luo added two thousand cavalry to him, which he regarded as too few;
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen and Mo Luo had long been at odds. Ordered to join the campaign, he grew more resentful still. Claiming that his forces were too weak, he received two thousand additional cavalry from Mo Luo—yet still deemed them insufficient.

sentences.zh: 又以馬疲瘠不任用搖軍心，軍無鬥志。

translations.literal: He also said the horses were worn thin and lean and unusable, shaking army morale, and the troops had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: He further complained that the horses were worn out and unfit for service, undermining morale until the army lost all fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 十二月，莫洛至寧羌，兩營相去二里許。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Mo Luo reached Ningqiang; the two camps were about two li apart.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Mo Luo reached Ningqiang, his camp and Fuchen's standing about two li apart.

sentences.zh: 先是，上命莫洛統綠營步旅下四川，嗣慮巴蜀道險，令貝勒洞鄂率滿洲騎兵兼程繼進。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had ordered Mo Luo to lead Green Standard infantry down into Sichuan; afterward, fearing the dangerous roads of Ba and Shu, he ordered Prince Dong'e to lead Manchu cavalry to follow by forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had ordered Mo Luo to lead Green Standard infantry into Sichuan. Fearing the treacherous Ba-Shu routes, he then ordered Prince Dong'e to follow with Manchu cavalry by forced marches.

sentences.zh: 軍未至，是月庚寅朔，癸巳，輔臣煽所部噪餉，襲劫莫洛。

translations.literal: The army had not yet arrived; on the first day gengyin of that month, on guisi, Fuchen incited his troops to clamor for pay and raided Mo Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Before reinforcements arrived, on the guisi day of that month Fuchen incited his men to riot for back pay and attacked Mo Luo.

sentences.zh: 莫洛督兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: Mo Luo directed the troops and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Luo led his troops and repulsed the assault.

sentences.zh: 甫定，輔臣复率悍黨至，砲矢雨坌，莫洛被創，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Just as things settled, Fuchen again led fierce partisans forward; cannonballs and arrows fell like rain; Mo Luo was wounded and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had order been restored when Fuchen returned at the head of his hard fighters. Cannon and musket fire poured down like rain. Mo Luo was wounded and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 卹典久未行，二十二年，命予祭葬，諡忠愍，授世職拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Funeral rites were long not carried out; in the twenty-second year, he was ordered to be granted sacrificial burial, posthumous title Zhongmin, and a hereditary office of baturalaburuhan together with tosahalaburuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral honors were long delayed. In 1683 he was granted state sacrifices and burial, given the posthumous title Zhongmin (Loyal and Commiserated), and his family received the hereditary ranks of baturalaburuhan and tosahalaburuhan.

sentences.zh: 子常安，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chang'an inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang'an inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: =陳福=陳福，字箕演，陝西榆林人。

translations.literal: =Chen Fu= Chen Fu, style Jiyan, a native of Yulin in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fu, styled Jiyan, was a native of Yulin in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 國初師定陝西，福以武舉應募，從寧夏總兵劉芳名剿寇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty, when the army pacified Shaanxi, Fu enrolled as a military licentiate and followed Ningxia regional commander Liu Fangming in suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty's armies pacified Shaanxi, Fu enrolled as a military licentiate and served under Ningxia Regional Commander Liu Fangming in suppressing bandits.

sentences.zh: 敘功，授守備。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was appointed garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was appointed garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 又從都統李國翰下四川，遷遵義游擊。

translations.literal: He again followed commandant Li Guohan into Sichuan and was transferred to be a roving-attacker at Zunyi.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Commandant Li Guohan into Sichuan and was transferred to roving-attacker at Zunyi.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，從總督李國英討李自成遺黨郝搖旗、李來亨等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi, he followed governor-general Li Guoying in campaigning against Li Zicheng's remnant followers Hao Yaoqi, Li Laiheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign he served under Governor-General Li Guoying against Li Zicheng's remnant followers Hao Yaoqi, Li Laiheng, and others.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加右都督銜，擢成都副將，遷重慶總兵。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; he was given the brevet rank of right commissioner-in-chief, promoted to deputy regional commander at Chengdu, and transferred to regional commander at Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he received the brevet rank of Right Commissioner-in-Chief, was promoted to deputy regional commander at Chengdu, and later transferred to regional commander at Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入覲，授寧夏總兵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he came to court and was appointed regional commander at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In 1673 he presented himself at court and was appointed Regional Commander at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，鄭蛟麟以四川叛應之，遣使誘福。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui rebelled; Zheng Jiaolin rebelled in Sichuan in response and sent an envoy to entice Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Zheng Jiaolin rose in Sichuan in support and sent envoys to win Fu over.

sentences.zh: 福家留重慶，弟奇官守備，妻子亦在賊中，賊以是劫福。

translations.literal: Fu's family remained at Chongqing; his younger brother Qi held the post of garrison commander; wife and children were also in rebel hands; the rebels used this to coerce Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's family had remained in Chongqing. His younger brother Qi was a garrison commander, and his wife and children were in rebel hands. The rebels used them to pressure him.

sentences.zh: 福執其使，具疏入告，遣其弟諸生壽齎詣京師。

translations.literal: Fu seized their envoy, prepared a memorial reporting fully, and sent his younger brother, a student Shou, to carry it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fu arrested the envoy, memorialized the court in full, and sent his younger brother Shou, a licentiate, to deliver the report to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 上嘉福忠，授拜他喇布勒哈番，並官壽主事。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Fu's loyalty, granted baturalaburuhan, and also appointed Shou as a director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended Fu's loyalty, granted him the rank of baturalaburuhan, and appointed Shou as a director in the ministries.

sentences.zh: 輔臣據平涼，福上戰守方略。

translations.literal: Fuchen held Pingliang; Fu submitted strategies for fighting and defending.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuchen held Pingliang, Fu submitted plans for offense and defense.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢陝西提督，進三等阿思哈尼哈番，又官奇參將。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was promoted to Shaanxi provincial military commander, advanced to third-rank ashanihanihan, and his younger brother Qi was also made deputy regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1675 he was promoted to Provincial Military Commander of Shaanxi, advanced to third-rank ashanihanihan, and his brother Qi was made deputy regional commander.

sentences.zh: 進規花馬池，惠安、安定、定邊諸城堡，以次皆下。

translations.literal: He advanced to invest Huamachi, the fortresses of Hui'an, Anding, Dingbian and others, and in succession all fell.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Huamachi and the fortresses of Hui'an, Anding, Dingbian, and others, which fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 上擢壽鴻臚寺少卿。

translations.literal: The emperor promoted Shou to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promoted Shou to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 福率副將泰必圖乘勝薄固原，圍之匝月。

translations.literal: Fu led deputy regional commander Taibitu to press the victory close to Guyuan and besieged it for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: Fu led Deputy Regional Commander Taibitu in a victorious push against Guyuan and besieged the city for a full month.

sentences.zh: 輔臣遣其將來援，城賊亦突出，泰必圖戰死。

translations.literal: Fuchen sent his generals to relieve it; the rebels in the city also sallied forth; Taibitu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen sent reinforcements, and the garrison sallied out as well. Taibitu was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 福引兵還靈州，斬逃將賈從哲、張元經以徇。

translations.literal: Fu led the army back to Lingzhou and executed the deserter generals Jia Congzhe and Zhang Yuanjing as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Fu withdrew to Lingzhou and executed the fleeing generals Jia Congzhe and Zhang Yuanjing as an example.

sentences.zh: 上命福佐貝勒洞鄂攻平涼。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Fu to assist Prince Dong'e in attacking Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Fu to assist Prince Dong'e in the attack on Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 福疏言固原有賊萬餘，若我兵徑趨平涼，慮賊斷我餉道，當先取固原，上韙之。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized that at Guyuan there were more than ten thousand rebels; if our troops went straight toward Pingliang, he feared the rebels would cut our supply route; Guyuan should be taken first; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized that Guyuan held more than ten thousand rebels and that marching straight on Pingliang risked having supply lines cut. Guyuan must be taken first. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，福督兵取固原。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Fu directed the troops to take Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Fu led the assault on Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 天寒大雪，士卒苦遠役，且懲前敗，有戒心。

translations.literal: The weather was cold with heavy snow; the soldiers suffered from distant service, and having been chastened by the earlier defeat, they were on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter cold and heavy snow afflicted the troops on the long march. Chastened by the earlier defeat, they fought with caution.

sentences.zh: 是月甲寅朔，乙亥，師次惠安，下令：「五鼓會食，集城下，後者斬。

translations.literal: On the first day jiayin of that month, on yihai, the army halted at Hui'an; he issued an order: "At the fifth watch assemble to eat, gather below the city; those who come late are to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of that month the army halted at Hui'an. Fu ordered, "At the fifth watch take your meal and assemble below the walls. Latecomers will be executed.

sentences.zh: 」夜半時，參將熊虎等鼓譟入，刺福死。

translations.literal: " At midnight, deputy regional commander Xiong Hu and others beat drums and clamored as they entered and stabbed Fu to death.
translations.idiomatic: " At midnight Deputy Regional Commander Xiong Hu and others raised a mutiny, broke in, and stabbed Fu to death.

sentences.zh: 上以趙良棟代，收虎及首謀把總劉德及營兵戕福者悉誅之，贈福三等公，以三等精奇尼哈番世襲，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: The emperor replaced him with Zhao Liangdong, arrested Hu and the chief plotter platoon commander Liu De and all the camp soldiers who had killed Fu and executed them all; Fu was posthumously granted third-rank duke, with third-rank jingqinihanihan as a hereditary title, posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replaced him with Zhao Liangdong, arrested Xiong Hu, the ringleader Platoon Commander Liu De, and all the mutineers who had killed Fu, and had them executed. Fu was posthumously made a third-rank duke with a hereditary third-rank jingqinihanihan and given the posthumous title Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 建祠寧夏。

translations.literal: A shrine was built at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial shrine was built for him at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 擢奇天津總兵。

translations.literal: Qi was promoted to regional commander at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was promoted to Regional Commander at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 時福子世琳、世勳並陷賊，命以壽子世怡襲爵。

translations.literal: At the time Fu's sons Shilin and Shixun were both trapped among the rebels; he was ordered that Shou's son Shiyi should inherit the rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's sons Shilin and Shixun were then trapped in rebel territory, so the court ordered that Shou's son Shiyi should inherit the rank.

sentences.zh: 事定，壽棄官入四川求福妻子，得之遵義山中，將入都，上召世琳入見，問母子流離狀，深愍之，命襲爵，改籍寧夏。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Shou resigned office and entered Sichuan to seek Fu's wife and children; he found them in the mountains of Zunyi; as they were about to enter the capital, the emperor summoned Shilin to audience, asked about the mother and son's wandering and separation, was deeply moved with compassion, ordered him to inherit the rank, and changed his household register to Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended, Shou resigned his post and went into Sichuan to find Fu's wife and children. He discovered them in the mountains near Zunyi. As they were about to enter the capital, the emperor summoned Shilin and asked about the family's ordeal. Deeply moved, he ordered Shilin to inherit the rank and registered the family at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 旋授直隸三屯協副將。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed deputy regional commander of the Santun Brigade in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Deputy Regional Commander of the Santun Brigade in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 累遷古北鎮總兵、鑾儀使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to regional commander at Gubei Pass and director of imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Regional Commander at Gubei Pass and Director of Imperial Equipage.

sentences.zh: 世琳子益，益子大用，相繼襲爵。

translations.literal: Shilin's son Yi, and Yi's son Dayong, inherited the rank in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin's son Yi and Yi's son Dayong inherited the rank in turn.

sentences.zh: 益官至楚姚鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Yi reached the post of regional commander at Chuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Yi rose to Regional Commander at Chuyao.

sentences.zh: 大用乾隆間官江南提督，所屬游擊楊天相，獲海盜，總督蘇凌阿讞以為誣，誅天相，大用亦被譴。

translations.literal: Dayong in the Qianlong period held the post of Jiangnan provincial military commander; his subordinate roving-attacker Yang Tianxiang captured pirates; governor-general Su Ling'a judged it to be a false charge and executed Tianxiang; Dayong was also reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign Dayong served as Provincial Military Commander of Jiangnan. His subordinate Roving-Attacker Yang Tianxiang captured pirates, but Governor-General Su Ling'a ruled the case a fabrication, had Yang executed, and reprimanded Dayong as well.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，予守備銜，休致。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaqing, he was given the brevet rank of garrison commander and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiaqing reign he received the brevet rank of garrison commander and retired.

sentences.zh: =王之鼎=王之鼎，字公定，漢軍正紅旗人。

translations.literal: =Wang Zhiding= Wang Zhiding, style Gongding, a Chinese Bannerman of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiding, styled Gongding, was a Chinese Bannerman of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 父世選，仕明為參將。

translations.literal: His father Shixuan served the Ming as a deputy regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shixuan had served the Ming as a deputy regional commander.

sentences.zh: 歸太宗，授三等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: He submitted to Taizong and was granted third-rank angbang janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted to Taizong and was granted the third-rank title angbang janggin.

sentences.zh: 從世祖入關，徵江南有功，進二等。

translations.literal: He followed Shizu in entering the passes, had merit in campaigning in Jiangnan, and was advanced to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Shizu Emperor through the passes into China and distinguished himself in the Jiangnan campaigns, advancing to second rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，之鼎襲，進一等精奇尼哈番，署參領。

translations.literal: On his death, Zhiding inherited, was advanced to first-rank jingqinihanihan, and acted as company commander.
translations.idiomatic: On his death Zhiding inherited the rank, was advanced to first-rank jingqinihanihan, and served as acting company commander.

sentences.zh: 從貝勒屯齊徵湖南，擊走李定國、孫可望。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Tunqi in campaigning in Hunan and drove off Li Dingguo and Sun Kewang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Tunqi in the Hunan campaign and drove off Li Dingguo and Sun Kewang.

sentences.zh: 授正紅旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice commander-in-chief of the Chinese Bannermen of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Chinese Bannermen of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 駐防貴州。

translations.literal: He was stationed on garrison duty in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted on garrison duty in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，授福建中路總兵，討鄭錦，克廈門、金門、古浪諸島。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, he was appointed regional commander of the Middle Route in Fujian, campaigned against Zheng Jing, and captured Xiamen, Jinmen, Gulang and other islands.
translations.idiomatic: In 1662 he was appointed Regional Commander of Fujian's Middle Route, campaigned against Zheng Jing, and captured Xiamen, Jinmen, Gulang, and other islands.

sentences.zh: 三年，敗錦將黃盛、林茂、裴德等，拔銅山衛，進三等伯。

translations.literal: In the third year, he defeated Jing's generals Huang Sheng, Lin Mao, Pei De and others, took Tongshan Guard, and was advanced to third-rank earl.
translations.idiomatic: In 1664 he defeated Jing's generals Huang Sheng, Lin Mao, and Pei De, captured Tongshan Guard, and was advanced to third-rank earl.

sentences.zh: 八年，召還，仍授本旗副都統。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was recalled and again appointed vice commander-in-chief of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1669 he was recalled and reappointed Vice Commander-in-Chief of his banner.

sentences.zh: 十年，授江南提督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Jiangnan provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1671 he was appointed Provincial Military Commander of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授鎮海將軍，駐守京口。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was appointed Pacifier of the Sea general and garrisoned at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1673 he was appointed Pacifier of the Sea General and stationed at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂、耿精忠相繼反。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui and Geng Jingzhong rebelled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui and Geng Jingzhong rose in rebellion one after another.

sentences.zh: 上命之鼎分兵防安慶，而以安南將軍華善帥師佐之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhiding to divide troops to defend Anqing, while General of Pacifying the South Huashan led an army to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhiding to detach troops to defend Anqing while General Huashan of Pacifying the South led a force to assist him.

sentences.zh: 之鼎調崇明沙船，江陰、瓜洲戰艦，扼津要，令綠旗水師駐黃浦操防，兼備水陸。

translations.literal: Zhiding deployed Chongming sand boats and warships of Jiangyin and Guazhou to hold the strategic crossings, ordered Green Standard naval forces to garrison Huangpu for drill and defense, and prepared both land and water forces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiding deployed Chongming sand boats and warships from Jiangyin and Guazhou to hold key crossings, stationed Green Standard naval forces at Huangpu for drill and defense, and prepared for both land and river warfare.

sentences.zh: 上命簡親王喇佈為揚威大將軍，駐江寧，之鼎贊軍事。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Prince Jian Labu as grand general of awe-inspiring might, garrisoned at Jiangning; Zhiding assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Prince Jian Labu Grand General of Awe-Inspiring Might, stationed at Jiangning, with Zhiding assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十七年，改福建水師提督，加定海將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was changed to Fujian naval provincial military commander and given the additional title of Pacifier of Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In 1678 he was transferred to Provincial Military Commander of the Fujian Naval Forces with the additional title Pacifier of Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 閩寇日蹙，而楚、蜀間軍事方亟，請移鎮要地自效。

translations.literal: The Fujian rebels were daily pressed tighter, but military affairs between Chu and Shu were still urgent; he requested transfer to a strategic post to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels in Fujian were daily being cornered, but fighting in Huguang and Sichuan remained fierce. He asked to be transferred to a more critical post where he could serve.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調四川提督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was transferred to Sichuan provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1679 he was transferred to Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十九年，到官，會寇犯永寧，遂率總兵李芳述等討之，戰屢勝。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, he took office; rebels invaded Yongning; he thereupon led regional commander Li Fangshu and others to campaign against them and won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: In 1680 he assumed office. When rebels attacked Yongning, he led Regional Commander Li Fangshu and others against them and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 六月，勇略將軍趙良棟將進剿雲、貴，調芳述守敘州，之鼎留鎮永寧。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Valiant Strategy General Zhao Liangdong was about to advance to suppress Yunnan and Guizhou; Fangshu was transferred to defend Xuzhou; Zhiding remained to garrison Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Valiant Strategy General Zhao Liangdong prepared to advance into Yunnan and Guizhou. Fangshu was transferred to hold Xuzhou while Zhiding remained to garrison Yongning.

sentences.zh: 九月，吳世璠遣將尤廷玉、胡國柱攻永寧，圍之數匝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wu Shifan sent generals You Tingyu and Hu Guozhu to attack Yongning and surrounded it in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wu Shifan sent Generals You Tingyu and Hu Guozhu to attack Yongning and surrounded the city in tight rings.

sentences.zh: 時城中糧盡已兩閱月，之鼎猶率兵挑戰，士氣倍奮。

translations.literal: At the time grain in the city had been exhausted for two months already; Zhiding still led the troops to offer battle, and morale was doubly roused.
translations.idiomatic: Grain in the city had been exhausted for two months, yet Zhiding still led sorties against the enemy and morale remained high.

sentences.zh: 嗣為賊诇知，築長圍以守。

translations.literal: Afterward the rebels learned through scouts and built long encirclements to hold the siege.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels learned of the city's weakness through scouts, they built long siege lines and settled in to starve it out.

sentences.zh: 至是月甲子，寇穴城入，總兵費雅達，副將楊三虎，游擊週尚功，守備李逢春、魯明芝、席豹督兵巷戰，皆死。

translations.literal: On jiazi of that month, the rebels tunneled into the city; regional commander Fei Yada, deputy regional commander Yang Sanhu, roving-attacker Zhou Shanggong, garrison commanders Li Fengchun, Lu Mingzhi and Xi Bao directed troops in street fighting and all died.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of that month the rebels tunneled into the city. Regional Commander Fei Yada, Deputy Regional Commander Yang Sanhu, Roving-Attacker Zhou Shanggong, and Garrison Commanders Li Fengchun, Lu Mingzhi, and Xi Bao led street fighting and all perished.

sentences.zh: 之鼎解印付家人，令間道走成都，率總兵楊魁、何成德、王永世、傅汝友，游擊陳先鳳、陳田、劉應科等出禦賊，身受重創。

translations.literal: Zhiding removed his seal and gave it to his household, ordered them to take a bypath to flee to Chengdu, led regional commanders Yang Kui, He Chengde, Wang Yongshi, Fu Ruyou, roving-attackers Chen Xianfeng, Chen Tian, Liu Yingke and others out to resist the rebels, and himself received grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiding handed his seal to his household and ordered them to flee by a secret route to Chengdu. He led Regional Commanders Yang Kui, He Chengde, Wang Yongshi, and Fu Ruyou and Roving-Attackers Chen Xianfeng, Chen Tian, and Liu Yingke out to meet the enemy and was gravely wounded.

sentences.zh: 賊湧至，之鼎自度不能免，拔劍自刎，未殊，與魁等俱被執，傳送貴陽。

translations.literal: The rebels surged forward; Zhiding judged that he could not escape, drew his sword and cut his throat; before he died, he together with Kui and others were all seized and sent under escort to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels closed in, Zhiding judged that escape was impossible, drew his sword, and cut his throat. Before he died he was seized together with Yang Kui and the others and sent under escort to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 賊黨夏國相等百計誘降，之鼎厲聲叱曰：「死則死耳，肯向鼠輩乞活耶？

translations.literal: The rebel partisan Xia Guoxiang and others used a hundred schemes to entice him to surrender; Zhiding sternly shouted, saying: "To die is to die—would I beg life from such vermin?
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders such as Xia Guoxiang tried every means to win him over. Zhiding shouted, "Death is death—would I beg my life from such vermin?

sentences.zh: 」久之，賊知不可奪，遂遇害。

translations.literal: " After a long time, the rebels knew he could not be won over and thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " In time the rebels saw he could not be swayed and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 魁等皆不屈死。

translations.literal: Kui and the others all died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kui and the others likewise refused to submit and were killed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈之鼎太子少保，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Zhiding was posthumously granted junior guardian of the heir apparent and posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Zhiding was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhongyi (Loyal and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 子毓賢，官至貴州布政使，毓秀襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yuxian reached the post of Guizhou provincial administration commissioner; Yuxiu inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuxian rose to Guizhou Provincial Administration Commissioner; Yuxiu inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: =費雅達=費雅達，漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: =Fei Yada= Fei Yada, a Chinese Bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yada was a Chinese Bannerman of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自整儀尉累遷潼關副將。

translations.literal: From director of ceremonial guards he was promoted in succession to deputy regional commander at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Director of Ceremonial Guards to Deputy Regional Commander at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 王輔臣叛，廷議設漢中總兵討賊，以授費雅達，署都督僉事。

translations.literal: When Wang Fuchen rebelled, the court deliberated on establishing a Hanzhong regional commander to suppress the rebels and gave the post to Fei Yada, with acting rank of regional vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Fuchen rebelled, the court decided to create a Regional Commander post at Hanzhong to suppress the rebels and appointed Fei Yada, with acting rank of Regional Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 進取漢中，破賊彝門鎮，抵秦嶺，拔北木城，與王進寶會師奪武關。

translations.literal: He advanced to take Hanzhong, defeated the rebels at Yimen Town, reached the Qin Mountains, captured Beimu Fortress, and joined Wang Jinbao to retake Wu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced into Hanzhong, routed the rebels at Yimen Town, reached the Qin Mountains, captured Beimu Fortress, and joined Wang Jinbao to retake Wu Pass.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加都督同知。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was given the rank of regional vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Regional Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 永寧之役，城陷身死，贈左都督、太子少傅，諡忠勇。

translations.literal: In the Yongning campaign, when the city fell he died in body; he was posthumously granted left regional commander and junior tutor of the heir apparent, posthumous title Zhongyong.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongning, when the city fell he died in battle. He was posthumously made Left Regional Commander and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhongyong.

sentences.zh: 魁等皆予卹。

translations.literal: Kui and the others were all granted funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kui and the others likewise received funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 從三虎等戰死者，又有千總蔣得福、趙鳴鳳、王英傑；

translations.literal: Among those who died fighting with Sanhu and others were also battalion commanders Jiang Defu, Zhao Mingfeng and Wang Yingjie;
translations.idiomatic: Among those who fell with Yang Sanhu were Battalion Commanders Jiang Defu, Zhao Mingfeng, and Wang Yingjie.

sentences.zh: 從之鼎死者，又有從軍廕生潘濟世：並卹如例。

translations.literal: Among those who died with Zhiding was also the military student by hereditary privilege Pan Jishi: all were granted funeral rites according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who died with Zhiding was the military student Pan Jishi. All received funeral honors according to precedent.

sentences.zh: =李興元=李興元，字若始，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: =Li Xingyuan= Li Xingyuan, style Ruoshi, a Chinese Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingyuan, styled Ruoshi, was a Chinese Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 以拔貢授直隸沙河知縣，報最，遷祁州。

translations.literal: By selected tribute graduate he was appointed magistrate of Shahe in Zhili; at the evaluation he ranked highest and was transferred to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a selected tribute graduate he was appointed magistrate of Shahe in Zhili. Rated highest at evaluation, he was transferred to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 歷江西吉安、直隸永平知府，晉陝西隴右道。

translations.literal: He served in succession as prefect of Ji'an in Jiangxi and Yongping in Zhili, and was promoted to Longyou circuit intendant in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Ji'an in Jiangxi and Yongping in Zhili, then was promoted to Longyou Circuit Intendant in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，授雲南按察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi, he was appointed Yunnan provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1672 he was appointed Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 其明年，詔敕有司審理平西籓下逃兵。

translations.literal: The next year, an edict ordered the officials to try and judge deserters under the Pacification of the West feudatory.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict ordered local officials to try deserters from Wu Sangui's Pacification of the West domain.

sentences.zh: 時平西勳莊棋布，管莊者殺人奪貨，滋為民患。

translations.literal: At the time the merit estates of the Pacification of the West were spread like chess pieces; those who managed the estates killed people and seized goods, increasingly becoming a scourge to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's merit estates were scattered across the province like chess pieces. Their managers killed and plundered, becoming a growing scourge on the people.

sentences.zh: 訟牒命、盜兩案，兵居半。

translations.literal: In lawsuits of homicide and theft, soldiers made up half the cases.
translations.idiomatic: In homicide and theft cases, soldiers accounted for half the dockets.

sentences.zh: 又勒平民為餘丁；

translations.literal: They also coerced commoners to serve as surplus soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: They also coerced commoners into serving as surplus soldiers.

sentences.zh: 不從，則曰：「是我逃兵也。

translations.literal: if they did not comply, they would say: "These are my deserters.
translations.idiomatic: If a man refused, they would say, "He is my deserter.

sentences.zh: 」稱貸重息，人或絲毫負，亦以「逃兵」誣之，有司亡誰何。

translations.literal: " They lent money at heavy interest; if someone owed even the slightest amount, they also falsely charged him as a "deserter," and the officials had no one to hold accountable.
translations.idiomatic: " They lent at usurious rates, and anyone who owed even a fraction could be branded a deserter. Officials dared not intervene.

sentences.zh: 興元素持風力，諗知劉昆強項，令為審事官。

translations.literal: Xingyuan had always held to strict integrity; knowing that Liu Kun was a strong-willed man, he appointed him as an officer for trying cases.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan was known for his integrity. Knowing Liu Kun to be a man of firm character, he appointed him to hear cases.

sentences.zh: 有犯者論如法，部民德之，而大忤三桂意。

translations.literal: When there were offenders they were judged according to law; the people of the department were grateful, but this greatly offended Sangui's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders were punished according to law. The people were grateful, but the policy deeply offended Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 三桂將叛，使冶者鑄印，昆诇知，白興元，興元啟巡撫硃國治，趣入告。

translations.literal: Sangui was about to rebel and had metalworkers cast seals; Kun learned through inquiry, reported to Xingyuan, and Xingyuan informed governor Zhu Guozhi, urging him to enter and report.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui was preparing to rebel, he had seals cast. Kun discovered this and informed Xingyuan, who urged Governor Zhu Guozhi to report to the court at once.

sentences.zh: 國治遲數日始發，為三桂邏卒所得，遂作亂。

translations.literal: Guozhi delayed several days before sending the report; it was obtained by Sangui's patrol soldiers, and rebellion thereupon broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhi delayed several days before dispatching the report. Wu Sangui's patrols intercepted it, and rebellion broke out.

sentences.zh: 召各官集議，以國治苛虐失民心，殺之；

translations.literal: He summoned all officials to assemble for deliberation, saying that Guozhi was harsh and cruel and had lost the people's hearts, and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the officials and, claiming Guozhi's harsh rule had lost the people's hearts, had him killed.

sentences.zh: 迫授興元偽職，興元叱之曰：「汝內為國戚，外封親王，受恩重矣，何叛為？

translations.literal: He forced Xingyuan to accept a rebel post; Xingyuan rebuked him, saying: "You are within a kinsman of the state and without enfeoffed as a prince; you have received heavy favor—why rebel?
translations.idiomatic: They tried to force a rebel post on Xingyuan. He rebuked Wu Sangui: "You are the emperor's kinsman and a enfeoffed prince, showered with favor—why rebel?

sentences.zh: 我為丈夫，義可殺不可辱，惟一死以報朝廷。

translations.literal: I am a man; in righteousness one may be killed but not insulted; I have only death to repay the court.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of honor. Righteousness permits death but not dishonor. I have only my life to offer the throne.

sentences.zh: 」三桂怒，杖而下之獄。

translations.literal: " Sangui was enraged, had him beaten with rods and cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: " Wu Sangui flew into a rage, had him beaten, and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 雲南知府高顯辰及昆皆不屈，旋以興元及昆戍騰越衛。

translations.literal: Yunnan prefect Gao Xianchen and Kun both would not yield; shortly afterward Xingyuan and Kun were sent to garrison at Tengyue Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan Prefect Gao Xianchen and Liu Kun likewise refused to submit. Xingyuan and Kun were then sent to garrison at Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 十八年，師克湖南，時三桂已死，其子世璠使刺殺興元。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the army captured Hunan; at the time Sangui was already dead; his son Shifan sent assassins to kill Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1679 government forces took Hunan. Wu Sangui was already dead, but his son Shifan sent assassins to kill Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 師困滇城，興元二子廕秀、奇秀亦被殺。

translations.literal: The army besieged the Yunnan capital; Xingyuan's two sons Yinxiu and Qixiu were also killed.
translations.idiomatic: As government forces besieged Yunnan, Xingyuan's sons Yinxiu and Qixiu were also murdered.

sentences.zh: 事定，其三子萃秀詣軍所申訴，巡撫王繼文上其狀，贈太常寺卿。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, his third son Cuixiu went to the army headquarters to lodge a complaint; governor Wang Jiwen reported his case upward, and Xingyuan was posthumously granted vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended, his third son Cuixiu appealed at army headquarters. Governor Wang Jiwen reported the case, and Xingyuan was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 萃秀官至安陸府知府。

translations.literal: Cuixiu reached the post of prefect of Anlu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cuixiu rose to Prefect of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 昆當興元未死，出避民間。

translations.literal: When Xingyuan had not yet died, Kun went out to hide among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: While Xingyuan still lived, Kun went into hiding among the people.

sentences.zh: 事定，复補登州同知，遷常德知府。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was again appointed subprefect of Dengzhou and transferred to prefect of Changde.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he was reappointed Subprefect of Dengzhou and later transferred to Prefect of Changde.

sentences.zh: =陳啟泰=陳啟泰，字大來，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: =Chen Qitai= Chen Qitai, style Dalai, a Chinese Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qitai, styled Dalai, was a Chinese Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，自貢生知直隸滑縣，有聲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, by tribute student he became magistrate of Huaxian in Zhili and gained a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1647, as a tribute student, he became magistrate of Huaxian in Zhili and earned a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 行取，擢御史。

translations.literal: By special selection he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for central service, he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「滿洲部院官凡遇親喪，宜離任守制，以廣孝治。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Manchu officials in the ministries and boards who encounter a parent's death should leave office to observe mourning, in order to extend rule by filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Manchu officials in the ministries who suffer a parent's death should leave office to observe mourning, thereby extending the reign of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十一年，出為蘇松糧道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he went out as grain intendant of Suzhou and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1654 he was appointed Grain Intendant of Suzhou and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，調福建漳南道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi, he was transferred to Zhangnan circuit in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1664 he was transferred to Zhangnan Circuit in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉巡海道。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to coastal patrol intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1669 he was transferred to Coastal Patrol Intendant.

sentences.zh: 時山寇遍受耿精忠劄，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: At the time mountain bandits everywhere received letters from Geng Jingzhong; the situation was menacing.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain bandits across the region were receiving messages from Geng Jingzhong, and the situation grew menacing.

sentences.zh: 啟泰嚴保甲，立團長，親督所司捕賊。

translations.literal: Qitai strictly enforced the baojia system, established group leaders, and personally supervised his subordinates in capturing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai enforced the baojia household system strictly, appointed group leaders, and personally supervised the capture of bandits.

sentences.zh: 有乾禁令者，輒痛繩以法，姦宄屏息。

translations.literal: Those who violated prohibitions were at once severely punished according to law; evildoers fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who broke the prohibitions was severely punished by law, and wrongdoing subsided.

sentences.zh: 十三年，精忠叛，偽檄至漳州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Jingzhong rebelled; a false proclamation reached Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1674 Geng Jingzhong rebelled, and his manifesto reached Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 啟泰密與海澄公黃梧議拒守，會梧病，精忠复招鄭錦為助。

translations.literal: Qitai secretly discussed holding out with Duke of Haicheng Huang Wu; Wu fell ill; Jingzhong again recruited Zheng Jing as aid.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai secretly planned resistance with Duke of Haicheng Huang Wu, but Wu fell ill. Jingzhong then recruited Zheng Jing as an ally.

sentences.zh: 啟泰自度不能守，語妻劉曰：「義不偷生，忠不附賊，死吾事也。

translations.literal: Qitai judged that he could not hold the city and said to his wife Liu: "In righteousness one does not steal life; in loyalty one does not attach to rebels—death is my affair.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the city could not be held, Qitai told his wife Liu, "Righteousness forbids clinging to life; loyalty forbids serving rebels. Death is my duty.

sentences.zh: 然死而妻子為僇，吾何以瞑？

translations.literal: Yet if I die and wife and children are slaughtered, how can I close my eyes?
translations.idiomatic: But if I die and my wife and children are slaughtered by the rebels, how can I rest in peace?

sentences.zh: 」劉請殉，家人皆原從死。

translations.literal: " Liu asked to die with him; the household all wished to follow in death.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu asked to die with him, and the entire household wished to follow.

sentences.zh: 乃以巨盎置酒下藥，劉及侍妾婢僕飲者二十一人。

translations.literal: Thereupon in a great basin he set out wine with poison added; Liu and concubines, maids and servants who drank numbered twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared a great bowl of poisoned wine. Liu, his concubines, maids, and servants—twenty-one in all—drank and died.

sentences.zh: 幼子方六歲，持觴拜而飲。

translations.literal: His youngest son was only six years old; holding the cup he bowed and drank.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son, only six years old, took a cup, bowed, and drank.

sentences.zh: 啟泰朝服坐堂皇，召僚屬與訣，引弓弦自絞死，僚屬為殯。

translations.literal: Qitai in court dress sat in the main hall, summoned his subordinates to take leave, drew a bowstring and strangled himself to death; the subordinates prepared his burial.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai put on his court robes, sat in the main hall, bade farewell to his staff, and hanged himself with a bowstring. His subordinates prepared his burial.

sentences.zh: 錦兵入，見置棺縱橫，皆垂淚。

translations.literal: Jing's troops entered, saw coffins set out in rows, and all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Jing's troops entered and saw the row of coffins, they wept.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈通政使，賜葬祭。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted commissioner of the Office of Transmission and granted burial sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Commissioner of the Office of Transmission and granted state burial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 啟泰子汝器，聞變，赴漳州迎喪，為鄭錦兵掠去。

translations.literal: Qitai's son Ruqi, hearing of the upheaval, went to Zhangzhou to receive the coffin and was seized by Zheng Jing's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai's son Ruqi, hearing of the disaster, went to Zhangzhou to recover the bodies but was captured by Zheng Jing's troops.

sentences.zh: 逾二年乃脫還，詣京師，上念其父子忠義，加贈工部侍郎，授汝器右通政。

translations.literal: After more than two years he escaped and returned, went to the capital; the emperor, mindful of the father and son's loyalty and righteousness, additionally granted vice minister of the Ministry of Works and appointed Ruqi right vice commissioner of transmission.
translations.idiomatic: After more than two years he escaped and reached Beijing. Moved by the family's loyalty, the emperor additionally granted Qitai the post of Vice Minister of Works and appointed Ruqi Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，复予啟泰諡忠毅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, Qitai was again given posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1694 Qitai was again given the posthumous title Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 建祠福州，御書「忠義流芳」為祠額。

translations.literal: A shrine was built at Fuzhou; the emperor's own brush wrote "Loyalty and Righteousness Flow Forever" as the shrine inscription.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was built at Fuzhou with the imperial inscription "Loyalty and Righteousness Flow Forever."

sentences.zh: 汝器官至安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Ruqi reached the post of Anhui governor.
translations.idiomatic: Ruqi rose to Governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 方精忠叛時，諸郡望風納叛；

translations.literal: When Jingzhong rebelled, the various prefectures at the sight of the wind submitted to rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, prefectures across Fujian surrendered at the first rumor.

sentences.zh: 所不肯以城降者，啟泰死漳州，總兵吳萬福死福寧。

translations.literal: those who would not surrender their cities were: Qitai, who died at Zhangzhou, and regional commander Wu Wanfu, who died at Funing.
translations.idiomatic: Those who refused to surrender their cities were Chen Qitai, who died at Zhangzhou, and Regional Commander Wu Wanfu, who died at Funing.

sentences.zh: 萬福，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Wanfu was a Chinese Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wanfu was a Chinese Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 初仕明為守備。

translations.literal: He first served the Ming as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served the Ming as a garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 崇德七年，師圍松山，從副將夏承德來歸，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongde, when the army besieged Songshan, he followed deputy regional commander Xia Chengde in coming over and was appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In 1632, when Qing forces besieged Songshan, he followed Deputy Regional Commander Xia Chengde in surrendering and was appointed niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 入關，從征李自成有功，累敘二等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: After entering the passes, he had merit in campaigning against Li Zicheng and was repeatedly recorded for second-rank adahahan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qing entered the passes, he distinguished himself against Li Zicheng and was repeatedly advanced to second-rank adahahan.

sentences.zh: 出為福寧總兵。

translations.literal: He went out as regional commander at Funing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regional Commander at Funing.

sentences.zh: 張煌言兵屢入，與總兵李長榮分路擊卻之，累進右都督，精忠叛，萬福嬰城固守，城破，死之，闔家被害。

translations.literal: Zhang Huangyan's troops repeatedly entered; together with regional commander Li Changrong he attacked along separate routes and drove them back; he was repeatedly advanced to right regional commander; when Jingzhong rebelled, Wanfu enclosed the city and held firm; when the city fell he died, and the whole family was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Huangyan's forces repeatedly raided the coast, Wanfu and Regional Commander Li Changrong drove them back along separate routes. He rose to Right Regional Commander. When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Wanfu held Funing to the last. When the city fell he was killed, and his entire family perished with him.

sentences.zh: 幕客孫墢、百總潘騰鳳並殉。

translations.literal: His secretaries Sun Bang and company commander Pan Tengfeng also died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His secretary Sun Bang and Company Commander Pan Tengfeng died with him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈萬福左都督、太子少保，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Wanfu was posthumously granted left regional commander and junior guardian of the heir apparent, posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Wanfu was posthumously made Left Regional Commander and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: =陳丹赤=陳丹赤，字獻之，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: =Chen Danchi= Chen Danchi, style Xianzhi, a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Danchi, styled Xianzhi, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 順治十七年舉人，選授重慶推官，攝府事，兼署夔州府。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi he became a provincial graduate, was selected and appointed investigating censor of Chongqing, acted in prefectural affairs, and concurrently acted for Kuizhou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of 1660, he was appointed investigating censor of Chongqing, acted as prefect, and concurrently administered Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 時張獻忠初滅，蜀東尚淪於賊，徵師四集，丹赤給餉不乏。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Xianzhong had just been destroyed; eastern Shu was still overrun by bandits; expeditionary armies gathered from four sides; Danchi supplied provisions without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong had just been destroyed, but eastern Sichuan was still overrun by bandits and expeditionary armies were gathering from all sides. Danchi kept supplies flowing without fail.

sentences.zh: 墾荒萊，緩刑禁，報最，遷刑部主事，再晉兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He opened wasteland for cultivation, eased penal prohibitions, ranked highest at evaluation, was transferred to director in the Ministry of Punishments, and was again promoted to director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He opened wasteland for cultivation, eased harsh penalties, ranked highest at evaluation, and was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments and then promoted to director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 出為浙江按察司僉事、分巡溫處道，署按察使。

translations.literal: He went out as vice commissioner of the Zhejiang provincial surveillance commission and circuit intendant of Wenzhou and Chuzhou, acting as surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission and Circuit Intendant of Wenzhou and Chuzhou, acting as Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，入覲，道山東。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, he came to audience, traveling through Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1674 he traveled to court through Shandong.

sentences.zh: 會吳三桂反，詔入覲官悉還治所。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui rebelled; an edict ordered all officials who had come to audience to return to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, an edict ordered all officials en route to court to return to their posts.

sentences.zh: 丹赤歸至東昌，聞耿精忠亦叛，亟間道還。

translations.literal: Danchi returned as far as Dongchang, heard that Geng Jingzhong had also rebelled, and hurried back by a secret route.
translations.idiomatic: Danchi reached Dongchang and learned that Geng Jingzhong had also rebelled. He hurried back by a secret route.

sentences.zh: 適平陽叛將司定猷構精忠兵偪瑞安，丹赤獨居城上，泣諭父老，誓與城存亡。

translations.literal: Just then the Pingyang rebel general Si Dingyou joined Jingzhong's troops to press on Ruian; Danchi alone stood on the city wall, weeping as he instructed the elders, swearing to live or die with the city.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang rebel Si Dingyou joined Geng Jingzhong's forces in pressing Ruian. Danchi stood alone on the walls, weeping as he addressed the elders and swore to live or die with the city.

sentences.zh: 海寇硃飛熊乘間肆掠，鄉民爭入城，總兵祖弘勳慾不納。

translations.literal: Sea bandit Zhu Feixiong seized the interval to plunder wildly; villagers scrambled to enter the city; regional commander Zu Hongxun wished not to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bandit Zhu Feixiong seized the moment to plunder. Villagers scrambled into the city, but Regional Commander Zu Hongxun wished to shut them out.

sentences.zh: 丹赤曰：「城以人為固，人以食為命。

translations.literal: Danchi said: "A city is made secure by its people; people take grain as their life.
translations.idiomatic: Danchi said, "A city is defended by its people, and people live by grain.

sentences.zh: 民輦粟入城，民即兵，食即餉。

translations.literal: When the people carry grain into the city, the people are the army and the food is the pay.
translations.idiomatic: When the people bring grain into the city, the people become soldiers and the grain becomes rations.

sentences.zh: 亟宜納之，與共守。

translations.literal: They should quickly be admitted to defend together.
translations.idiomatic: Admit them at once and defend the city together.

sentences.zh: 」於是來者數万。

translations.literal: " Thereupon those who came numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: " Tens of thousands entered the city.

sentences.zh: 寇湧至，攻南門甚亟，副將楊春芳忽撤兵去，人心洶懼。

translations.literal: The rebels surged forward and attacked the south gate with great urgency; deputy regional commander Yang Chunfang suddenly withdrew his troops and left; popular sentiment was turbulent with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels surged against the south gate. Deputy Regional Commander Yang Chunfang suddenly withdrew his troops, and panic spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 丹赤日馳牒乞援，晨夜徼循，以忠義厲士卒，皆感泣，願死守。

translations.literal: Danchi daily sent urgent dispatches begging for relief; morning and night he patrolled the defenses; with loyalty and righteousness he encouraged the soldiers; all were moved to tears and wished to die holding firm.
translations.idiomatic: Danchi sent daily dispatches begging for reinforcements and patrolled the defenses day and night. He roused the troops with talk of loyalty and righteousness until they wept and vowed to hold to the death.

sentences.zh: 弘勳將以溫州叛，陽遣游擊馬文始助守，實以诇丹赤，丹赤誓以身殉。

translations.literal: Hongxun was about to rebel with Wenzhou; outwardly he sent roving-attacker Ma Wenshi to help defend, but in fact to spy on Danchi; Danchi swore to die for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxun planned to surrender Wenzhou. He sent Roving-Attacker Ma Wenshi ostensibly to help defend but in fact to spy on Danchi. Danchi swore to die for the city.

sentences.zh: 六月甲午朔，弘勳陳甲仗華蓋山，集文武官計事，欲以脅丹赤。

translations.literal: On the first day jiawu of the sixth month, Hongxun arrayed arms at Huagai Mountain, gathered civil and military officials to deliberate, intending to coerce Danchi.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the sixth month Hongxun arrayed troops at Huagai Mountain and summoned the civil and military officials, intending to coerce Danchi.

sentences.zh: 千總姚紹英知其謀，勸勿往，丹赤不顧，策馬去。

translations.literal: Battalion commander Yao Shaoying knew his plot and urged him not to go; Danchi paid no heed and spurred his horse away.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion Commander Yao Shaoying learned of the plot and urged him not to go. Danchi ignored the warning and rode out.

sentences.zh: 至則兵露刃夾階立，坐定，弘勳曰：「彼眾我寡，將若何？

translations.literal: When he arrived, troops with bared blades stood flanking the steps; once seated, Hongxun said: "They are many and we are few—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, armed soldiers lined both sides of the steps. Hongxun said, "They are many and we are few. What shall we do?

sentences.zh: 」丹赤曰：「提標前鋒五千人已集，且民心效死，戰即不足，守自有餘。

translations.literal: " Danchi said: "The provincial commander's vanguard of five thousand men has already assembled, and the people's hearts are ready to die in service; for fighting it may not suffice, but for defense there is more than enough.
translations.idiomatic: " Danchi replied, "Five thousand vanguard troops of the provincial command are already assembled, and the people are ready to die for the city. We may lack strength to attack, but we have more than enough to defend.

sentences.zh: 吾此來商以舟濟師，顧乃計多寡邪？

translations.literal: I came here to discuss ferrying troops by boat—yet you are reckoning numbers?
translations.idiomatic: I came to discuss ferrying reinforcements by boat. Why are we counting numbers?

sentences.zh: 」弘勳曰：「舟安在？

translations.literal: " Hongxun said: "Where are the boats?
translations.idiomatic: " Hongxun asked, "Where are the boats?

sentences.zh: 」丹赤語通判白鼇宸曰：「河干泊舟不少，皆鄉民所棄。

translations.literal: " Danchi said to subprefect Bai Aochen: "Along the riverbank moored boats are not few; all were abandoned by the villagers.
translations.idiomatic: " Danchi turned to Subprefect Bai Aochen. "Many boats lie moored along the riverbank, abandoned by the villagers.

sentences.zh: 以濟援師，何患無舟？

translations.literal: Use them to ferry relief troops—what worry is there of lacking boats?
translations.idiomatic: Use them to ferry reinforcements. How can we lack boats?

sentences.zh: 」弘勳語塞，春芳厲聲言曰：「城中糧盡，縱有兵有舟，誰為我用？

translations.literal: " Hongxun was left speechless; Chunfang said in a harsh voice: "Grain in the city is exhausted; even if there are troops and boats, who will serve me?
translations.idiomatic: " Hongxun was silenced. Chunfang said harshly, "Grain in the city is exhausted. Even with troops and boats, who will fight for us?

sentences.zh: 」丹赤曰：「若言誤矣。

translations.literal: " Danchi said: "Your words are mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: " Danchi said, "You are mistaken.

sentences.zh: 吾軍糧餉足供六閱月，且遠近鄉民輸粟入。

translations.literal: Our army's grain and pay are sufficient for six months, and moreover villagers near and far are bringing grain in.
translations.idiomatic: Our rations will last six months, and villagers near and far are still bringing in grain.

sentences.zh: 若乃為此言惑軍心邪？

translations.literal: Are you speaking such words to shake army morale?
translations.idiomatic: Are you saying this to shake the army's morale?

sentences.zh: 」有自懷中出帛書者，精忠招弘勳獻城檄也，丹赤怒，碎而擲之地，曰：「此豈可污吾目？

translations.literal: " Someone produced a silk letter from his bosom—the proclamation by which Jingzhong recruited Hongxun to surrender the city; Danchi was enraged, tore it to pieces and threw it to the ground, saying: "How can this be allowed to stain my eyes?
translations.idiomatic: " Someone produced a silk letter from his sleeve—Geng Jingzhong's summons for Hongxun to surrender the city. Danchi tore it to pieces and flung it down. "How can I let this filth before my eyes?

sentences.zh: 吾頭可斷，城不可得也！

translations.literal: My head may be cut off, but the city cannot be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: My head may fall, but the city will not be surrendered!

sentences.zh: 」弘勳執其手，好語慰之，丹赤曰：「封疆之臣死封疆，不知其他。

translations.literal: " Hongxun took his hand and spoke soothing words to comfort him; Danchi said: "A minister of the frontier dies on the frontier—I know nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongxun took his hand and spoke soothingly. Danchi said, "A frontier official dies on the frontier. I know nothing else.

sentences.zh: 」弘勳知不可奪，目千總高魁持斧擁丹赤出，罵益厲，執斧者斷其臂，大呼曰：「臣事畢矣！

translations.literal: " Hongxun knew he could not be won over, signaled battalion commander Gao Kui holding an axe to seize Danchi and take him out; Danchi cursed all the more fiercely; the axe-bearer severed his arm; he shouted loudly: "A minister's duty is finished!
translations.idiomatic: " Seeing that Danchi could not be swayed, Hongxun signaled Battalion Commander Gao Kui, who seized him with an axe. Danchi cursed all the louder. Gao severed his arm. Danchi shouted, "My duty as a minister is done!

sentences.zh: 」兵刃交下，遂遇害。

translations.literal: " Blades crossed and struck down; he thereupon was killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Blades rained down on him, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 十六年，浙江巡撫陳秉直疏請卹，贈通政使，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Zhejiang governor Chen Bingzhi memorialized requesting funeral rites; he was posthumously granted commissioner of transmission, posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1677 Zhejiang Governor Chen Bingzhi memorialized for funeral honors. Danchi was posthumously made Commissioner of Transmission with the posthumous title Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上南巡，丹赤子一夔時為湖州知府，迎謁，上書額賜之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, the emperor made a southern tour; Danchi's son Yikui was then prefect of Huzhou; he came forward to audience; the emperor wrote an inscription and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1699, during an imperial southern tour, Danchi's son Yikui, then Prefect of Huzhou, came forward to audience and received an imperial inscription from the emperor's own brush.

sentences.zh: =馬閟=馬閟，字奉璋，陝西武功人。

translations.literal: =Ma Bi= Ma Bi, style Fengzhang, a native of Wugong in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Bi, styled Fengzhang, was a native of Wugong in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年舉人，授山東昌樂知縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the eleventh year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of Changle in Shandong and had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of 1654, he was appointed magistrate of Changle in Shandong and governed with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，補永嘉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, he was transferred to Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: In 1674 he was appointed magistrate of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 明決有才，清覈圖籍，不數月而政成。

translations.literal: Clear and decisive with talent, he examined land registers thoroughly; within a few months his administration was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Decisive and capable, he thoroughly audited the land registers, and within months his administration was in order.

sentences.zh: 華蓋山集議，弘勳戕丹赤，閟躍而起曰：「國家豢若輩，反黨賊殺封疆大吏，吾恥與若輩俱生！

translations.literal: At the assembly on Huagai Mountain, Hongxun killed Danchi; Bi leaped up and said: "The state has nurtured you people, yet you turn to rebel bandits and kill a frontier grand official—I am ashamed to live together with you!
translations.idiomatic: At the assembly on Huagai Mountain, Hongxun murdered Danchi. Bi leaped to his feet and cried, "The state has nurtured you, yet you side with rebels and murder a frontier minister. I am ashamed to breathe the same air as you!

sentences.zh: 」遂罵不絕口，同時遇害。

translations.literal: " He thereupon cursed without cease and was killed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: " He cursed without cease and was killed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈布政司參政。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted vice commissioner of the provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，敕建祠溫州，祀丹赤及閟，亦曰「雙忠」。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, by imperial order a shrine was built at Wenzhou to sacrifice to Danchi and Bi; it was also called "Twin Loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: In 1696 an imperial order built a shrine at Wenzhou honoring Danchi and Bi, called the Shrine of Twin Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上南巡，閟子逸姿官江南布政司參議督糧道，迎謁，疏引丹赤例求賜諡，上允之，諡忠勤，亦賜御書額如一夔。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, the emperor made a southern tour; Bi's son Yizi held the post of grain transport supervising participant in the Jiangnan provincial administration commission; he came forward to audience, memorialized citing Danchi's precedent to request a posthumous title; the emperor approved, posthumous title Zhongqin, and also bestowed an imperial inscription as with Yikui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1703, during an imperial southern tour, Bi's son Yizi, then Grain Transport Supervisor in the Jiangnan administration, came forward to audience and cited Danchi's precedent to request a posthumous title. The emperor granted the title Zhongqin and bestowed an imperial inscription as he had for Yikui.

sentences.zh: 丹赤役林莪、僕張亦寶，閟從子穎姿，皆從死。

translations.literal: Danchi's clerk Lin E, servant Zhang Yibao, and Bi's nephew Yingzi all followed in death.
translations.idiomatic: Danchi's clerk Lin E, his servant Zhang Yibao, and Bi's nephew Yingzi all died with their masters.

sentences.zh: =葉映榴=葉映榴，字炳霞，江南上海人。

translations.literal: =Ye Yingliu= Ye Yingliu, style Bingxia, a native of Shanghai in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yingliu, styled Bingxia, was a native of Shanghai in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治十八年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the eighteenth year of Shunzhi, he was selected as a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate of 1661, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 時方嚴治江南逋賦士紳，映榴在籍中，降國子監博士。

translations.literal: At the time they were strictly punishing gentry and officials in Jiangnan for overdue taxes; Yingliu was on the list and was demoted to doctor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was strictly pursuing Jiangnan gentry in arrears on taxes, Yingliu was on the list and was demoted to Doctor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出榷贛關，會吳三桂叛，贛南北路絕。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise the Ganzhou customs barrier; Wu Sangui rebelled; north-south routes through Ganzhou were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to supervise the Ganzhou customs post. When Wu Sangui rebelled, north-south traffic through Ganzhou was severed.

sentences.zh: 映榴與同官守險要，撫流民，境獲寧。

translations.literal: Yingliu together with his colleagues held strategic passes, comforted displaced people, and the region obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yingliu and his colleagues held the strategic passes, comforted displaced people, and restored order to the region.

sentences.zh: 提學陝西巡撫鄂愷薦其才，康熙二十四年，授湖廣糧儲道。

translations.literal: Educational intendant and Shaanxi governor E Kai recommended his talent; in the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi, he was appointed grain storage intendant of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Educational Intendant and Shaanxi Governor E Kai recommended his ability. In 1685 he was appointed Grain Storage Intendant of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 清積逋，減耗羨，事有不便於民者，輒與大吏力爭。

translations.literal: He cleared accumulated arrears, reduced surcharge surpluses; whenever something was not convenient for the people, he at once strove with the grand officials.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared accumulated tax arrears and reduced surcharge surpluses. Whenever a policy harmed the people, he fought the senior officials over it.

sentences.zh: 二十七年五月，廷議省湖廣總督，並裁督標兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-seventh year, the court deliberated on abolishing the Huguang governor-general and also cutting the governor's personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of 1688 the court decided to abolish the Huguang governor-generalship and disband the governor's personal troops.

sentences.zh: 楚兵素剽悍，有夏逢龍者，尤桀黠，能以小信義結其伍，隱附之。

translations.literal: Chu troops were by nature fierce and bold; there was one Xia Fenglong, especially fierce and cunning, who could bind his comrades with small acts of faith and righteousness and had secretly attached them to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang troops were notoriously fierce. One Xia Fenglong was especially cunning and had won the soldiers' trust through small favors, secretly gathering followers.

sentences.zh: 檄既下，裁兵洶洶亡所歸。

translations.literal: Once the proclamation was issued, the troops to be cut were turbulent and had nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Once the order was issued, the troops slated for discharge grew restive with nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 總督徐國相還朝已登舟，眾圍訴索餉，不得，遂大譁。

translations.literal: Governor-general Xu Guoxiang, returning to court, had already boarded his boat; the crowd surrounded him pleading for pay; they did not obtain it and thereupon raised a great clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Xu Guoxiang had already boarded his boat to return to court when the soldiers surrounded him demanding back pay. Denied, they raised a great uproar.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫柯永昇初上官，映榴攝布政使才三日。

translations.literal: At the time governor Ke Yongsheng had just taken office; Yingliu had acted as provincial administration commissioner for only three days.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ke Yongsheng had just assumed office. Yingliu had been acting provincial administration commissioner for only three days.

sentences.zh: 事急，映榴白永昇，請予兩月糧遣散，不許。

translations.literal: The matter was urgent; Yingliu informed Yongsheng, requesting that two months' grain be given to disperse them; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis mounted, Yingliu urged Yongsheng to grant two months' rations for discharge. Yongsheng refused.

sentences.zh: 眾入巡撫署，露刃呼譟。

translations.literal: The crowd entered the governor's yamen, bared blades and shouted in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers stormed the governor's yamen with bared blades, shouting and threatening.

sentences.zh: 映榴复白永昇，請好言慰遣之。

translations.literal: Yingliu again informed Yongsheng, requesting that soothing words be used to comfort and dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Yingliu again urged Yongsheng to speak gently and persuade them to disperse.

sentences.zh: 永昇出，眾語不遜，永昇曰：「若輩欲反邪？

translations.literal: Yongsheng came out; the crowd's words were insolent; Yongsheng said: "Do you people wish to rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Yongsheng came out to face them. When their words grew insolent, he said, "Do you mean to rebel?

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「反也奈何？

translations.literal: " The crowd said: "If we rebel, what of it?
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "And if we do—what then?

sentences.zh: 」刃傷永昇臂，奪其印，复刃傷足，僕，遂擁映榴至閱馬場。

translations.literal: " They wounded Yongsheng's arm with blades, seized his seal, again wounded his foot and servants, and thereupon seized Yingliu and took him to the horse-review ground.
translations.idiomatic: " They slashed Yongsheng's arm, seized his seal, wounded his foot and his servants, then seized Yingliu and dragged him to the horse-review ground.

sentences.zh: 永昇得間自經死。

translations.literal: Yongsheng found an interval and hanged himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yongsheng found a moment's opening and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 逢龍自號「總統兵馬大元帥」，幟以白，迫布政使以下官受偽職，映榴紿以無殺掠，三日後徐議之。

translations.literal: Fenglong styled himself "Grand Marshal Commanding All Forces," used white banners, compelled officials from the provincial administration commissioner downward to accept false posts; Yingliu deceived them with promises of no killing or plundering, to be discussed slowly after three days.
translations.idiomatic: Fenglong styled himself Grand Marshal Commanding All Forces and raised white banners. He forced officials down to the administration commissioner to accept rebel posts. Yingliu stalled them with promises of no killing or looting, asking for three days to consider.

sentences.zh: 乃令其妻陳奉母吳自水溝出，解印付其僕，乃手具遺疏。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered his wife Chen to escort his mother Wu out through the water ditch, removed his seal and gave it to his servant, and thereupon wrote the final memorial by hand.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his wife Chen to escort his mother Wu out through a water ditch, handed his seal to a servant, and wrote his final memorial by hand.

sentences.zh: 是月丁酉，朝服升公座，罵賊，拔佩刀自刎死。

translations.literal: On dingyou of that month, in court dress he ascended the public seat, cursed the rebels, drew his belt dagger and cut his throat to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of that month he put on court robes, took the official seat, cursed the rebels, and cut his throat with his belt dagger.

sentences.zh: 疏略曰：「臣一介豎儒，叨沐皇上高厚深恩，歷擢今職。

translations.literal: The memorial in summary said: "Your servant is a mere rustic scholar who has received the emperor's lofty, generous and profound favor and has been promoted in succession to my present post.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial read in part: "Your servant is but a humble scholar who has bathed in the emperor's profound grace and risen to my present post.
