sentences.zh: 嘗以潔己奉公，自矢夙夜，但媿才具庸劣，未效寸長。

translations.literal: I have sought to keep myself pure in serving the public and have pledged myself day and night, but I am ashamed that my talent is mediocre and inferior and I have not rendered the slightest merit.
translations.idiomatic: I have striven to keep myself pure in public service and to labor day and night, yet I am ashamed that my mediocre talents have rendered no real service.

sentences.zh: 茲值裁兵夏逢龍倡亂，劫奪撫臣敕印，分兵圍臣衙門，露刃逼脅。

translations.literal: Now, at the time of cutting troops, Xia Fenglong has raised disorder, seized the governor's imperial seal, divided troops to surround your servant's yamen, and with bared blades coerces and threatens.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as troops are being discharged, Xia Fenglong has risen in mutiny, seized the governor's seal, surrounded my yamen with armed men, and threatens me at blade's point.

sentences.zh: 臣幼讀詩書，粗知節義，雖斧鑕在前，豈肯喪恥偷生？

translations.literal: Your servant from youth read the classics and histories and roughly knows integrity and righteousness; though the axe and boiling cauldron lie before me, how could I lose shame and steal life?
translations.idiomatic: From youth I have read the classics and know something of integrity. Though execution awaits, how could I disgrace myself to cling to life?

sentences.zh: 臣母年七十有六，在臣任所；

translations.literal: Your servant's mother is seventy-six years old and is at your servant's post of duty;
translations.idiomatic: My mother is seventy-six and lives at my post;

sentences.zh: 臣長子旉，遠在原籍；

translations.literal: your servant's eldest son Fu is far away in the native place;
translations.idiomatic: my eldest son Fu is far away in our native place;

sentences.zh: 其餘二子尚未成童，煢煢孤嫠，死將安歸？

translations.literal: the remaining two sons have not yet reached boyhood; lonely and bereft, widows and orphans—if I die, whither shall they go?
translations.idiomatic: my other two sons are still children. Bereft widows and orphans—if I die, where shall they turn?

sentences.zh: 因遣妻女奉母潛逃。

translations.literal: Therefore I have sent wife and daughters to escort my mother in secret flight.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore sent my wife and daughters to escort my mother to safety in secret.

sentences.zh: 臣如微服匿影，或可倖免以圖後效。

translations.literal: If your servant were to don plain clothes and hide my shadow, I might perhaps escape by luck to plan later service.
translations.idiomatic: If I were to slip away in disguise, I might perhaps survive to serve again later.

sentences.zh: 伏念臣守土之官也，城存與存，城亡與亡，義所當然。

translations.literal: Prostrating myself, I reflect that your servant is an official who guards the soil: when the city exists I exist with it, when the city perishes I perish with it—this is righteousness as it must be.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I reflect that as an official charged with guarding this territory, I must live or die with the city. That is righteousness itself.

sentences.zh: 今勉盡一死，以報國恩。

translations.literal: Now I strive to exhaust one death to repay the state's favor.
translations.idiomatic: I shall now do my utmost to die once, and thereby repay the state's grace.

sentences.zh: 所恨事起倉猝，既不能先事綢繆，默消反側；

translations.literal: What I regret is that the affair arose in sudden haste: I could neither make prior arrangements to quietly dispel unrest;
translations.idiomatic: I regret only that the crisis came so suddenly: I could neither foresee it and quietly forestall the mutiny,

sentences.zh: 復不能臨期捍禦，獨守孤城。

translations.literal: nor at the critical moment defend and hold, guarding a lone city alone.
translations.idiomatic: nor at the last moment defend the city alone.

sentences.zh: 上辜三十載之皇恩，下棄七旬餘之老母，君親兩負，死有餘慚。

translations.literal: Above I fail the thirty years of imperial favor; below I abandon a mother of more than seventy years; sovereign and parent both I have failed—in death there is more than enough shame.
translations.idiomatic: I have failed the thirty years of imperial grace above and abandoned my mother of more than seventy below. I have failed both sovereign and parent. Even in death my shame is more than I can bear.

sentences.zh: 」上覽疏，深愍傷之，召廷臣展讀，聞者皆感泣。

translations.literal: " When the emperor read the memorial, he was deeply moved with compassion and grief; he summoned court ministers to read it aloud; all who heard were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor read the memorial, he was deeply moved. He summoned the court to hear it read aloud, and all who listened wept.

sentences.zh: 下部議卹，部議援陳丹赤例，贈通政使，特旨贈工部侍郎。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the ministries to deliberate on funeral rites; the ministry proposed citing Chen Danchi's precedent and granting commissioner of transmission; by special edict he was granted vice minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated on funeral honors and proposed citing Chen Danchi's precedent for posthumous Commissioner of Transmission. A special edict raised the grant to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 次年上南巡，旉迎謁，手書「忠節」二字賜之，遂以為諡。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor made a southern tour; Fu came forward to audience; the emperor's own brush wrote the two characters "Loyal Integrity" and bestowed them; this thereupon became his posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, during an imperial southern tour, Fu came forward to audience. The emperor wrote Loyal Integrity with his own brush and bestowed it as Yingliu's posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 立祠武昌，書「丹心炳冊」扁以賜。

translations.literal: A shrine was established at Wuchang; he wrote the plaque "Loyal Heart Shines in the Records" and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was built at Wuchang, and the emperor bestowed the plaque Loyal Heart Shines in the Records.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，錄忠臣後，授其子旉鳳陽知府；

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, descendants of loyal ministers were recorded; his son Fu was appointed prefect of Fengyang;
translations.idiomatic: In 1730, when the court enrolled descendants of loyal ministers, his son Fu was appointed Prefect of Fengyang;

sentences.zh: 芳蔚州知州，尋改員外郎；

translations.literal: Fang was made magistrate of Weizhou, and shortly afterward transferred to director;
translations.idiomatic: Fang was made Magistrate of Weizhou and later transferred to director in the ministries;

sentences.zh: 孫鳳毛內閣中書。

translations.literal: grandson Fengmao was made secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and grandson Fengmao was made a Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 與映榴同時死者，都司宣德仁，贈副將。

translations.literal: One who died at the same time as Yingliu was brigade vice commander Xuan Deren, posthumously granted deputy regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Deren, a brigade vice commander who died at the same time, was posthumously made Deputy Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：功令褒死事，倉卒遇變與艱難效死者同，所以獎忠義也。

translations.literal: =Commentary= The commentary says: The merit regulations honor death in service; meeting sudden change and dying in hard struggle are treated the same, in order to reward loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The merit regulations honor those who die in service. Whether death comes in sudden crisis or through prolonged hardship, the reward is the same—so that loyalty and righteousness may be encouraged.

sentences.zh: 莫洛與福，先事宜知有變，師行有進無退，雖死不撓。

translations.literal: Mo Luo and Fu ought beforehand to have known that change was coming; on campaign there is advance and no retreat; though they died, they did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Luo and Chen Fu should have foreseen trouble, yet on campaign they advanced without retreat and did not yield even in death.

sentences.zh: 之鼎效忠於孤城，興元抗節於大憝。

translations.literal: Zhiding showed loyalty in a lone city; Xingyuan upheld integrity against a great foe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiding proved loyal in a besieged city; Li Xingyuan held to his integrity against a mighty rebel.

sentences.zh: 若啟泰、丹赤、映榴，皆能死其官者。

translations.literal: As for Qitai, Danchi and Yingliu, all were able to die in their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qitai, Chen Danchi, and Ye Yingliu all died at their posts.

sentences.zh: 啟泰以其家殉，與馬雄鎮比烈；

translations.literal: Qitai sacrificed his whole household, comparable in fervor to Ma Xiongzhen;
translations.idiomatic: Qitai sacrificed his entire household, a fervor comparable to that of Ma Xiongzhen;

sentences.zh: 映榴遺疏款款，則又范承謨蒙谷自序之亞也。

translations.literal: Yingliu's final memorial, so earnest and sincere, is again next only to Fan Chengmo's Menggu self-preface.
translations.idiomatic: and Yingliu's earnest final memorial ranks next only to Fan Chengmo's Menggu self-preface.
